question: On Sunday 7 December 2025, Haitam died of a heart attack after being subdued by eight national police officers in Torremolinos. He was hit by Tasers – which can deliver up to 1 200 volts – at least three times. Images of the scene show police officers immobilising him and threating to taser him again, while cries of pain can be heard.

International bodies, including the European Committee for the Prevention of Torture, warn that electroshock weapons can cause death if used repeatedly or for prolonged immobilisation. In the past year, at least four other racialised people have died in police action, revealing a pattern of racist police violence.

This constitutes a breach by Spain of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and of the obligation to ensure proportional and accountable policing, as the Commission highlights in its rule of law reports. In light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission intend to ask the Spanish Government to provide explanations for those deaths?
Does it plan to specifically examine the use of Tasers by Member States’ police forces?
Does it intend to promote, at EU level, limitations on, or the ban of, Tasers, as well as greater obligations to monitor the use of force?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.3.2026) As the Commission set out in its reply to written questions E-003732/20201, E-005750/20202, any use of force by law enforcement authorities should always be exercised in a proportionate manner. In particular, Article 4 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU prohibits inhuman or degrading treatment of any individual.

In order to support Member States in preventing discriminatory profiling practices, under the EU Anti-Racism Strategy, the Commission will compile a compendium of good practices8. Maintenance of law and order, including the use of tasers, is primarily a national competence.

Member States must promote and ensure respect of fundamental rights as provided for in their constitutional order, and in line with their European and international human rights obligations. In the case referred to by the Honourable Member, it is therefore for the Spanish authorities to conduct independent investigations.
